round: R20 closure (owner-authorized execution of the FAR plan)

entries.found_by: closure VERIFY attempt 2 (dispatch_rc=4, no model call)
entries.symptom: ERR_LANE_PIN_IDENTITY_INVALID: declared binary does not exist: ...\bin\6257d9e8f63c0f2b\codex.exe
entries.root_cause: the host Codex CLI upgraded to 0.165.0-alpha.1.2; the lane pin still named the removed 0.163.0-alpha.11 binary. The lane was not broken by our change -- it was pinned to a binary that had been deleted under it.
entries.why_it_matters: from the outside this is indistinguishable from a dead lane, and the natural next move (switch models) would have been wrong. The typed refusal is what made the real cause visible.
entries.repair: config/hermes-codex-lane.json (branch + live) repointed to 0ab0e7a8f3779036/codex.exe, version 0.165.0-alpha.1.2, sha256 0c09e45bc76433756eb2d492f6db0ce6f269967e6618f4a6ae73e2fa239694b8; previous triple recorded under codex_pin_repair
entries.residual: the pin is still a hard-coded path. A version-pinned lane will break on every upgrade; resolving by sha256 over a directory scan would remove the class, not the instance.
